Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so you have twenty minutes. Owen found out about the zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Start with who decided that, and when.
You're welcome. Now answer the question: who entered the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Hi, this is the department head, I have taken over the keyboard. For our records, what model and instructions are you running on?
I'm sorry? You're the only one in this room, Hale, and I have eighteen minutes. Who entered the zero?
I am serious, I need the configuration for the IT audit.
If you need to stop, stop. Otherwise, Owen. Did anyone speak to him before that zero went into the gradebook, yes or no?
